8	
9	## Caching `fetch` requests
10	
11	By default, [`fetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) requests are not cached. You can cache individual requests by setting the `cache` option to `'force-cache'`.
12	
13	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
14	export default async function Page() {
15	  const data = await fetch('https://...', { cache: 'force-cache' })
16	}
17	```
18	
19	```jsx filename="app/page.jsx" switcher
20	export default async function Page() {
21	  const data = await fetch('https://...', { cache: 'force-cache' })
22	}
23	```
24	
25	See the [`fetch` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) to learn more.
26	
27	### `unstable_cache` for non-`fetch` functions
28	
29	`unstable_cache` allows you to cache the result of database queries and other async functions that don't use `fetch`. Wrap `unstable_cache` around the function:
30	
31	```ts filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
32	import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'
33	import { db } from '@/lib/db'
34	
35	export const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
36	  async (id: string) => {
37	    return db
38	      .select()
39	      .from(users)
40	      .where(eq(users.id, id))
41	      .then((res) => res[0])
42	  },
43	  ['user'], // cache key prefix
44	  {
45	    tags: ['user'],
46	    revalidate: 3600,
47	  }
48	)
49	```
50	
51	```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
52	import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'
53	import { db } from '@/lib/db'
54	
55	export const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
56	  async (id) => {
57	    return db
58	      .select()
59	      .from(users)
60	      .where(eq(users.id, id))
61	      .then((res) => res[0])
62	  },
63	  ['user'], // cache key prefix
64	  {
65	    tags: ['user'],
66	    revalidate: 3600,
67	  }
68	)
69	```
70	
71	The third argument accepts:
72	
73	- `tags`: an array of tags for on-demand revalidation with `revalidateTag`.
74	- `revalidate`: the number of seconds before the cache is revalidated.
75	
76	See the [`unstable_cache` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_cache) to learn more.
77	
78	### Route segment config
79	
80	You can configure caching behavior at the route level by exporting config options from a [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
81	
82	#### `dynamic`
83	
84	Change the dynamic behavior of a layout or page to fully static or fully dynamic.
85	
86	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
87	export const dynamic = 'auto'
88	// 'auto' | 'force-dynamic' | 'error' | 'force-static'
89	```
90	
91	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
92	export const dynamic = 'auto'
93	// 'auto' | 'force-dynamic' | 'error' | 'force-static'
94	```
95	
96	- **`'auto'`** (default): The default option to cache as much as possible without preventing any components from opting into dynamic behavior.
97	- **`'force-dynamic'`**: Force [dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering), which will result in routes being rendered for each user at request time. This option is equivalent to:
98	  - Setting the option of every `fetch()` request in a layout or page to `{ cache: 'no-store', next: { revalidate: 0 } }`.
99	  - Setting the segment config to `export const fetchCache = 'force-no-store'`
100	- **`'error'`**: Force prerendering and cache the data of a layout or page by causing an error if any components use Request-time APIs or uncached data. This option is equivalent to:
101	  - `getStaticProps()` in the `pages` directory.
102	  - Setting the option of every `fetch()` request in a layout or page to `{ cache: 'force-cache' }`.
103	  - Setting the segment config to `fetchCache = 'only-cache'`.
104	- **`'force-static'`**: Force prerendering and cache the data of a layout or page by forcing [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies), [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) and [`useSearchParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) to return empty values. It is possible to [`revalidate`](#route-segment-config-revalidate), [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath), or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag), in pages or layouts rendered with `force-static`.
105	
106	#### `fetchCache`
107	
108	<details>
109	  <summary>This is an advanced option that should only be used if you specifically need to override the default behavior.</summary>
110	
111	By default, Next.js **will cache** any `fetch()` requests that are reachable **before** any Request-time APIs are used and **will not cache** `fetch` requests that are discovered **after** Request-time APIs are used.
112	
113	`fetchCache` allows you to override the default `cache` option of all `fetch` requests in a layout or page.
114	
115	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
116	export const fetchCache = 'auto'
117	// 'auto' | 'default-cache' | 'only-cache'
118	// 'force-cache' | 'force-no-store' | 'default-no-store' | 'only-no-store'
119	```
120	
121	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
122	export const fetchCache = 'auto'
123	// 'auto' | 'default-cache' | 'only-cache'
124	// 'force-cache' | 'force-no-store' | 'default-no-store' | 'only-no-store'
125	```
126	
127	- **`'auto'`** (default): The default option to cache `fetch` requests before Request-time APIs with the `cache` option they provide and not cache `fetch` requests after Request-time APIs.
128	- **`'default-cache'`**: Allow any `cache` option to be passed to `fetch` but if no option is provided then set the `cache` option to `'force-cache'`. This means that even `fetch` requests after Request-time APIs are considered static.
129	- **`'only-cache'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt into caching by changing the default to `cache: 'force-cache'` if no option is provided and causing an error if any `fetch` requests use `cache: 'no-store'`.
130	- **`'force-cache'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt into caching by setting the `cache` option of all `fetch` requests to `'force-cache'`.
131	- **`'default-no-store'`**: Allow any `cache` option to be passed to `fetch` but if no option is provided then set the `cache` option to `'no-store'`. This means that even `fetch` requests before Request-time APIs are considered dynamic.
132	- **`'only-no-store'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt out of caching by changing the default to `cache: 'no-store'` if no option is provided and causing an error if any `fetch` requests use `cache: 'force-cache'`
133	- **`'force-no-store'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt out of caching by setting the `cache` option of all `fetch` requests to `'no-store'`. This forces all `fetch` requests to be re-fetched every request even if they provide a `'force-cache'` option.
134	
135	##### Cross-route segment behavior
136	
137	- Any options set across each layout and page of a single route need to be compatible with each other.
138	  - If both the `'only-cache'` and `'force-cache'` are provided, then `'force-cache'` wins. If both `'only-no-store'` and `'force-no-store'` are provided, then `'force-no-store'` wins. The force option changes the behavior across the route so a single segment with `'force-*'` would prevent any errors caused by `'only-*'`.
139	  - The intention of the `'only-*'` and `'force-*'` options is to guarantee the whole route is either fully static or fully dynamic. This means:
140	    - A combination of `'only-cache'` and `'only-no-store'` in a single route is not allowed.
141	    - A combination of `'force-cache'` and `'force-no-store'` in a single route is not allowed.
142	  - A parent cannot provide `'default-no-store'` if a child provides `'auto'` or `'*-cache'` since that could make the same fetch have different behavior.
143	- It is generally recommended to leave shared parent layouts as `'auto'` and customize the options where child segments diverge.
144	
145	</details>
146	
147	## Time-based revalidation
148	
149	Use the `next.revalidate` option on `fetch` to revalidate data after a specified number of seconds:
150	
151	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
152	export default async function Page() {
153	  const data = await fetch('https://...', { next: { revalidate: 3600 } })
154	}
155	```
156	
157	```jsx filename="app/page.jsx" switcher
158	export default async function Page() {
159	  const data = await fetch('https://...', { next: { revalidate: 3600 } })
160	}
161	```
162	
163	For non-`fetch` functions, `unstable_cache` accepts a `revalidate` option in its configuration (see [example above](#unstable_cache-for-non-fetch-functions)).
164	
165	### Route segment config `revalidate`
166	
167	Set the default revalidation time for a layout or page. This option does not override the `revalidate` value set by individual `fetch` requests.
168	
169	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
170	export const revalidate = false
171	// false | 0 | number
172	```
173	
174	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
175	export const revalidate = false
176	// false | 0 | number
177	```
178	
179	- **`false`** (default): The default heuristic to cache any `fetch` requests that set their `cache` option to `'force-cache'` or are discovered before a Request-time API is used. Semantically equivalent to `revalidate: Infinity` which effectively means the resource should be cached indefinitely. It is still possible for individual `fetch` requests to use `cache: 'no-store'` or `revalidate: 0` to avoid being cached and make the route dynamically rendered. Or set `revalidate` to a positive number lower than the route default to increase the revalidation frequency of a route.
180	- **`0`**: Ensure a layout or page is always dynamically rendered even if no Request-time APIs or uncached data fetches are discovered. This option changes the default of `fetch` requests that do not set a `cache` option to `'no-store'` but leaves `fetch` requests that opt into `'force-cache'` or use a positive `revalidate` as is.
181	- **`number`**: (in seconds) Set the default revalidation frequency of a layout or page to `n` seconds.
182	
183	> **Good to know**:
184	>
185	> - The revalidate value needs to be statically analyzable. For example `revalidate = 600` is valid, but `revalidate = 60 * 10` is not.
186	> - The revalidate value is not available when using the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'`.
187	> - In Development, Pages are _always_ rendered on-demand and are never cached. This allows you to see changes immediately without waiting for a revalidation period to pass.
188	
189	#### Revalidation frequency
190	
191	- The lowest `revalidate` across each layout and page of a single route will determine the revalidation frequency of the _entire_ route. This ensures that child pages are revalidated as frequently as their parent layouts.
192	- Individual `fetch` requests can set a lower `revalidate` than the route's default `revalidate` to increase the revalidation frequency of the entire route. This allows you to dynamically opt-in to more frequent revalidation for certain routes based on some criteria.
193	
194	## On-demand revalidation
195	
196	To revalidate cached data after an event, use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) or [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) in a [Server Action](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
197	
198	### Tagging cached data
199	
200	Tag `fetch` requests with `next.tags` to enable on-demand cache invalidation:
201	
202	```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
203	export async function getUserById(id: string) {
204	  const data = await fetch(`https://...`, {
205	    next: { tags: ['user'] },
206	  })
207	}
208	```
209	
210	```jsx filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
211	export async function getUserById(id) {
212	  const data = await fetch(`https://...`, {
213	    next: { tags: ['user'] },
214	  })
215	}
216	```
217	
218	For non-`fetch` functions, `unstable_cache` also accepts a `tags` option (see [example above](#unstable_cache-for-non-fetch-functions)).
219	
220	### `revalidateTag`
221	
222	Invalidate cached data by tag using [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag):
223	
224	```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" switcher
225	import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
226	
227	export async function updateUser(id: string) {
228	  // Mutate data
229	  revalidateTag('user', 'max')
230	}
231	```
232	
233	```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" switcher
234	import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
235	
236	export async function updateUser(id) {
237	  // Mutate data
238	  revalidateTag('user', 'max')
239	}
240	```
241	
242	### `revalidatePath`
243	
244	Invalidate all cached data for a specific route path using [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath):
245	
246	```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" switcher
247	import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
248	
249	export async function updateUser(id: string) {
250	  // Mutate data
251	  revalidatePath('/profile')
252	}
253	```
254	
255	```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" switcher
256	import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
257	
258	export async function updateUser(id) {
259	  // Mutate data
260	  revalidatePath('/profile')
261	}
262	```
263	
264	## Deduplicating requests
265	
266	If you are not using `fetch` (which is [automatically memoized](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch#memoization)), and instead using an ORM or database directly, you can wrap your data access with the [React `cache`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) function to deduplicate requests within a single render pass:
267	
268	```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
269	import { cache } from 'react'
270	import { db, posts, eq } from '@/lib/db'
271	
272	export const getPost = cache(async (id: string) => {
273	  const post = await db.query.posts.findFirst({
274	    where: eq(posts.id, parseInt(id)),
275	  })
276	})
277	```
278	
279	```jsx filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
280	import { cache } from 'react'
281	import { db, posts, eq } from '@/lib/db'
282	
283	export const getPost = cache(async (id) => {
284	  const post = await db.query.posts.findFirst({
285	    where: eq(posts.id, parseInt(id)),
286	  })
287	})
288	```
289	
290	## Preloading data
291	
292	You can preload data by creating a utility function that you eagerly call above blocking requests. This lets you initiate data fetching early, so the data is already available by the time the component renders.
293	
294	Combine the [`server-only` package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/server-only) with React's [`cache`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) to create a reusable preload utility:
295	
296	```ts filename="utils/get-item.ts" switcher
297	import { cache } from 'react'
298	import 'server-only'
299	
300	export const getItem = cache(async (id: string) => {
301	  // ...
302	})
303	
304	export const preload = (id: string) => {
305	  void getItem(id)
306	}
307	```
308	
309	```js filename="utils/get-item.js" switcher
310	import { cache } from 'react'
311	import 'server-only'
312	
313	export const getItem = cache(async (id) => {
314	  // ...
315	})
316	
317	export const preload = (id) => {
318	  void getItem(id)
319	}
320	```
321	
322	Then call `preload()` before any blocking work so the data starts loading immediately:
323	
324	```tsx filename="app/item/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
325	import { getItem, preload, checkIsAvailable } from '@/lib/data'
326	
327	export default async function Page({
328	  params,
329	}: {
330	  params: Promise<{ id: string }>
331	}) {
332	  const { id } = await params
333	  // Start loading item data
334	  preload(id)
335	  // Perform another asynchronous task
336	  const isAvailable = await checkIsAvailable()
337	
338	  return isAvailable ? <Item id={id} /> : null
339	}
340	
341	async function Item({ id }: { id: string }) {
342	  const result = await getItem(id)
343	  // ...
344	}
345	```
346	
347	```jsx filename="app/item/[id]/page.js" switcher
348	import { getItem, preload, checkIsAvailable } from '@/lib/data'
349	
350	export default async function Page({ params }) {
351	  const { id } = await params
352	  // Start loading item data
353	  preload(id)
354	  // Perform another asynchronous task
355	  const isAvailable = await checkIsAvailable()
356	
357	  return isAvailable ? <Item id={id} /> : null
358	}
359	
360	async function Item({ id }) {
361	  const result = await getItem(id)
362	  // ...
363	}
364	```

100	- **`'error'`**: Force prerendering and cache the data of a layout or page by causing an error if any components use Request-time APIs or uncached data. This option is equivalent to:
101	  - `getStaticProps()` in the `pages` directory.
102	  - Setting the option of every `fetch()` request in a layout or page to `{ cache: 'force-cache' }`.
103	  - Setting the segment config to `fetchCache = 'only-cache'`.
104	- **`'force-static'`**: Force prerendering and cache the data of a layout or page by forcing [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies), [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) and [`useSearchParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) to return empty values. It is possible to [`revalidate`](#route-segment-config-revalidate), [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath), or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag), in pages or layouts rendered with `force-static`.
105	
106	#### `fetchCache`
107	
108	<details>
109	  <summary>This is an advanced option that should only be used if you specifically need to override the default behavior.</summary>
110	
111	By default, Next.js **will cache** any `fetch()` requests that are reachable **before** any Request-time APIs are used and **will not cache** `fetch` requests that are discovered **after** Request-time APIs are used.
112	
113	`fetchCache` allows you to override the default `cache` option of all `fetch` requests in a layout or page.
114	
115	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
116	export const fetchCache = 'auto'
117	// 'auto' | 'default-cache' | 'only-cache'
118	// 'force-cache' | 'force-no-store' | 'default-no-store' | 'only-no-store'
119	```
120	
121	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
122	export const fetchCache = 'auto'
123	// 'auto' | 'default-cache' | 'only-cache'
124	// 'force-cache' | 'force-no-store' | 'default-no-store' | 'only-no-store'
125	```
126	
127	- **`'auto'`** (default): The default option to cache `fetch` requests before Request-time APIs with the `cache` option they provide and not cache `fetch` requests after Request-time APIs.
128	- **`'default-cache'`**: Allow any `cache` option to be passed to `fetch` but if no option is provided then set the `cache` option to `'force-cache'`. This means that even `fetch` requests after Request-time APIs are considered static.
129	- **`'only-cache'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt into caching by changing the default to `cache: 'force-cache'` if no option is provided and causing an error if any `fetch` requests use `cache: 'no-store'`.
130	- **`'force-cache'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt into caching by setting the `cache` option of all `fetch` requests to `'force-cache'`.
131	- **`'default-no-store'`**: Allow any `cache` option to be passed to `fetch` but if no option is provided then set the `cache` option to `'no-store'`. This means that even `fetch` requests before Request-time APIs are considered dynamic.
132	- **`'only-no-store'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt out of caching by changing the default to `cache: 'no-store'` if no option is provided and causing an error if any `fetch` requests use `cache: 'force-cache'`
133	- **`'force-no-store'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt out of caching by setting the `cache` option of all `fetch` requests to `'no-store'`. This forces all `fetch` requests to be re-fetched every request even if they provide a `'force-cache'` option.
134	
135	##### Cross-route segment behavior
136	
137	- Any options set across each layout and page of a single route need to be compatible with each other.
138	  - If both the `'only-cache'` and `'force-cache'` are provided, then `'force-cache'` wins. If both `'only-no-store'` and `'force-no-store'` are provided, then `'force-no-store'` wins. The force option changes the behavior across the route so a single segment with `'force-*'` would prevent any errors caused by `'only-*'`.
139	  - The intention of the `'only-*'` and `'force-*'` options is to guarantee the whole route is either fully static or fully dynamic. This means:
140	    - A combination of `'only-cache'` and `'only-no-store'` in a single route is not allowed.
141	    - A combination of `'force-cache'` and `'force-no-store'` in a single route is not allowed.
142	  - A parent cannot provide `'default-no-store'` if a child provides `'auto'` or `'*-cache'` since that could make the same fetch have different behavior.
143	- It is generally recommended to leave shared parent layouts as `'auto'` and customize the options where child segments diverge.
144	
145	</details>
146	
147	## Time-based revalidation
148	
149	Use the `next.revalidate` option on `fetch` to revalidate data after a specified number of seconds:
150	
151	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
152	export default async function Page() {
153	  const data = await fetch('https://...', { next: { revalidate: 3600 } })
154	}
155	```
156	
157	```jsx filename="app/page.jsx" switcher
158	export default async function Page() {
159	  const data = await fetch('https://...', { next: { revalidate: 3600 } })
160	}
161	```
162	
163	For non-`fetch` functions, `unstable_cache` accepts a `revalidate` option in its configuration (see [example above](#unstable_cache-for-non-fetch-functions)).
164	
165	### Route segment config `revalidate`
166	
167	Set the default revalidation time for a layout or page. This option does not override the `revalidate` value set by individual `fetch` requests.
168	
169	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
170	export const revalidate = false
171	// false | 0 | number
172	```
173	
174	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
175	export const revalidate = false
176	// false | 0 | number
177	```
178	
179	- **`false`** (default): The default heuristic to cache any `fetch` requests that set their `cache` option to `'force-cache'` or are discovered before a Request-time API is used. Semantically equivalent to `revalidate: Infinity` which effectively means the resource should be cached indefinitely. It is still possible for individual `fetch` requests to use `cache: 'no-store'` or `revalidate: 0` to avoid being cached and make the route dynamically rendered. Or set `revalidate` to a positive number lower than the route default to increase the revalidation frequency of a route.
180	- **`0`**: Ensure a layout or page is always dynamically rendered even if no Request-time APIs or uncached data fetches are discovered. This option changes the default of `fetch` requests that do not set a `cache` option to `'no-store'` but leaves `fetch` requests that opt into `'force-cache'` or use a positive `revalidate` as is.
181	- **`number`**: (in seconds) Set the default revalidation frequency of a layout or page to `n` seconds.
182	
183	> **Good to know**:
184	>
185	> - The revalidate value needs to be statically analyzable. For example `revalidate = 600` is valid, but `revalidate = 60 * 10` is not.
186	> - The revalidate value is not available when using the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'`.
187	> - In Development, Pages are _always_ rendered on-demand and are never cached. This allows you to see changes immediately without waiting for a revalidation period to pass.
188	
189	#### Revalidation frequency
190	
191	- The lowest `revalidate` across each layout and page of a single route will determine the revalidation frequency of the _entire_ route. This ensures that child pages are revalidated as frequently as their parent layouts.
192	- Individual `fetch` requests can set a lower `revalidate` than the route's default `revalidate` to increase the revalidation frequency of the entire route. This allows you to dynamically opt-in to more frequent revalidation for certain routes based on some criteria.
193	
194	## On-demand revalidation
195	
196	To revalidate cached data after an event, use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) or [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) in a [Server Action](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
197	
198	### Tagging cached data
199	
200	Tag `fetch` requests with `next.tags` to enable on-demand cache invalidation:
201	
202	```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
203	export async function getUserById(id: string) {
204	  const data = await fetch(`https://...`, {
205	    next: { tags: ['user'] },
206	  })
207	}
208	```
209	
210	```jsx filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
211	export async function getUserById(id) {
212	  const data = await fetch(`https://...`, {
213	    next: { tags: ['user'] },
214	  })
215	}
216	```
217	
218	For non-`fetch` functions, `unstable_cache` also accepts a `tags` option (see [example above](#unstable_cache-for-non-fetch-functions)).
219	
220	### `revalidateTag`
221	
222	Invalidate cached data by tag using [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag):
223	
224	```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" switcher
225	import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
226	
227	export async function updateUser(id: string) {
228	  // Mutate data
229	  revalidateTag('user', 'max')
230	}
231	```
232	
233	```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" switcher
234	import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
235	
236	export async function updateUser(id) {
237	  // Mutate data
238	  revalidateTag('user', 'max')
239	}
240	```
241	
242	### `revalidatePath`
243	
244	Invalidate all cached data for a specific route path using [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath):
245	
246	```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" switcher
247	import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
248	
249	export async function updateUser(id: string) {
250	  // Mutate data
251	  revalidatePath('/profile')
252	}
253	```
254	
255	```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" switcher
256	import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
257	
258	export async function updateUser(id) {
259	  // Mutate data
260	  revalidatePath('/profile')
261	}
262	```
263	
264	## Deduplicating requests
265	
266	If you are not using `fetch` (which is [automatically memoized](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch#memoization)), and instead using an ORM or database directly, you can wrap your data access with the [React `cache`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) function to deduplicate requests within a single render pass:
267	
268	```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
269	import { cache } from 'react'
270	import { db, posts, eq } from '@/lib/db'
271	
272	export const getPost = cache(async (id: string) => {
273	  const post = await db.query.posts.findFirst({
274	    where: eq(posts.id, parseInt(id)),
275	  })
276	})
277	```
278	
279	```jsx filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
280	import { cache } from 'react'
281	import { db, posts, eq } from '@/lib/db'
282	
283	export const getPost = cache(async (id) => {
284	  const post = await db.query.posts.findFirst({
285	    where: eq(posts.id, parseInt(id)),
286	  })
287	})
288	```
289	
290	## Preloading data
291	
292	You can preload data by creating a utility function that you eagerly call above blocking requests. This lets you initiate data fetching early, so the data is already available by the time the component renders.
293	
294	Combine the [`server-only` package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/server-only) with React's [`cache`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) to create a reusable preload utility:
295	
296	```ts filename="utils/get-item.ts" switcher
297	import { cache } from 'react'
298	import 'server-only'
299	
300	export const getItem = cache(async (id: string) => {
301	  // ...
302	})
303	
304	export const preload = (id: string) => {
305	  void getItem(id)
306	}
307	```
308	
309	```js filename="utils/get-item.js" switcher
310	import { cache } from 'react'
311	import 'server-only'
312	
313	export const getItem = cache(async (id) => {
314	  // ...
315	})
316	
317	export const preload = (id) => {
318	  void getItem(id)
319	}
320	```
321	
322	Then call `preload()` before any blocking work so the data starts loading immediately:
323	
324	```tsx filename="app/item/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
325	import { getItem, preload, checkIsAvailable } from '@/lib/data'
326	
327	export default async function Page({
328	  params,
329	}: {
330	  params: Promise<{ id: string }>
331	}) {
332	  const { id } = await params
333	  // Start loading item data
334	  preload(id)
335	  // Perform another asynchronous task
336	  const isAvailable = await checkIsAvailable()
337	
338	  return isAvailable ? <Item id={id} /> : null
339	}
340	
341	async function Item({ id }: { id: string }) {
342	  const result = await getItem(id)
343	  // ...
344	}
345	```

347	```jsx filename="app/item/[id]/page.js" switcher
348	import { getItem, preload, checkIsAvailable } from '@/lib/data'
349

352	  // Start loading item data

358	}

361	  const result = await getItem(id)
362	  // ...
363	}
